cards.explanation: The answer is a meal with her table set. Next comes the food: Wisdom has prepared her meat, mixed her wine and set her table. Her house is built and dinner is ready. I've pulled a batch out of the oven with the doorbell already ringing, so a host with the table set gets my respect, friends.

The answer is False. Wisdom doesn't wait for anyone to stumble on her house. She sends out her maidservants and calls out from the heights of the city (Proverbs 9:3). Her invitation goes out to the people, which is a lot more work than sitting by the door with the lights on.

The answer is the simple who lack judgment. Wisdom says, “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” and she says it to him who lacks judgment. The invitation goes to the people who don't have it all figured out yet. I qualify on a good day, and the door is open to me too.

The answer is your folly. Wisdom says, “Leave your folly behind, and you will live; walk in the way of understanding.” The only thing she asks you to drop at the door is the folly. Bring your appetite and leave that at home. I once tried to carry too many trays at once, and believe me, friends, putting something down is sometimes the smartest move.

The word is live. Wisdom says, “Leave your folly behind, and you will live…” Her invitation comes with a promise of life. A host who sets a table and then promises life to the guests, that's a good invitation.

The answer is that he brings shame on himself. The passage says, “He who corrects a mocker brings shame on himself…” The one who steps up to correct a mocker walks away with shame. Sometimes the kindest move is to save your breath and keep your own apron clean.

The answer is True. The passage says, “rebuke a wise man, and he will love you.” (Proverbs 9:8) The wise man will love the one who rebukes him. Compare that with the mocker, who, the verse says, will hate you. It's a good reminder to be the wise one when a correction comes my way.
The answer is the fear of the LORD. The passage says, “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom…” That's where wisdom starts. Not at the end of a long climb, but at the very first step.

The word is years. The passage says, “For through wisdom your days will be multiplied, and years will be added to your life.” Days multiplied and years added, it's a double promise. I'll take extra time in the bakery any day.

The two words are wise and scoff. “If you are wise, you are wise to your own advantage…” The benefit lands right on the one who chooses wisdom, like a good batch you get to eat yourself. The verse goes on, “but if you scoff, you alone will bear the consequences.” The weight lands on the scoffer alone, friends, and nobody else gets handed that bill.

The answer is True. The passage says, “She sits at the door of her house…” (Proverbs 9:14). Folly has her own house, just like Wisdom. Both women have a place and both are calling people to it. That's what makes this choice a tricky one.

The word is same. Folly says, “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” and Wisdom said those same words in Proverbs 9:4. The opening words are an exact match. I think that's worth slowing down for, friends.

The answer is that bread eaten in secret is tasty. Folly says, “Stolen water is sweet, and bread eaten in secret is tasty!” Notice how the pitch leans on secrecy and stealing. It sounds exciting, but the verse right after tells the rest.

The answer is the dead, and it's a heavy one. The passage says the dead are there, and that her guests are in the depths of Sheol (Proverbs 9:18). Her pitch sounds sweet and tasty, but that's what's inside. I think this is a serious line, and it's worth sitting with.

The answer is False. The passage says, “But they do not know that the dead are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.” The ones she invites don't know. It's a heavy verse, and it shows why Wisdom's call matters.
